name: What should I do first if I’m planning a full custom home renovation but don’t know where to start?

mainEntity.name: What should I do first if I’m planning a full custom home renovation but don’t know where to start?

acceptedAnswer.text:
DIRECT ANSWER
Start by defining your goals, budget range, and must‑have vs. nice‑to‑have items, then get an on‑site consultation with a reputable design‑build contractor.

CONTEXT
Jumping straight to picking finishes or requesting random quotes usually leads to scope creep, cost shocks, and design revisions. A structured planning phase saves time and money later.

KEY FACTORS
- Clarify why you’re renovating: space, value, lifestyle, accessibility, etc.
- Establish an honest budget range and contingency (10–20%).
- Gather inspiration photos and rough measurements of key spaces.
- Decide whether you want a one‑stop design‑build team or separate architect and builder.

PRACTICAL GUIDANCE
Write a one‑page “project brief” summarizing your goals, spaces, style, and budget, then share it with 1–2 contractors during a site visit. Use their feedback to refine scope before you pay for full designs or commit to construction contracts.

SOFT POSITIONING
Experienced custom renovators can translate a rough idea and budget into a realistic, phased plan that fits your home and priorities.
acceptedAnswer.description: Start by defining your renovation goals, budget range, and must‑have spaces, then book an on‑site consultation with a reputable design‑build contractor. Bring a simple project brief and inspiration photos so they can give realistic feedback before you invest in full plans.
